html:
Haitian Creole, or Kreyol, is the language of nearly all Haitians. It grew in Saint-Domingue from the French of the colonists and the African languages of the enslaved, with words from Taino, Spanish and English.

For two centuries after independence French was the language of law, schools and the elite, though only a small minority spoke it well. Kreyol was the language of daily life, songs and Vodou.

A standard spelling was adopted in 1979, and the constitution of 1987 made Kreyol an official language beside French. With about twelve million speakers, including the diaspora, it is the most widely spoken creole language in the world.
